acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Wraiths family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Wraith, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Orbit-Blade Boundary Hunter (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A clearly defined robed and hooded figure with fully visible skeletal hands, a spectral blade with a solid-looking hilt, and three rusted chains orbiting the body above a vapor tail.

Signature mechanic: Borrowed Edge: three orbiting chains sweep the room until one link touches a wall, pillar, or shield. The Wraith passes only the spectral blade through that marked boundary, causing its edge to emerge along the entire touched line while the robed body and hilt remain fixed. Severing the contacting chain or striking the hilt collapses the remote edge.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the floor into boundary prediction by orbiting several chains around a fully defined spectral blade and choosing one contacted surface as the blade's remote emergence edge.
constructionDimensions: The T1 Shade holds cinder flecks and soot-dark hot vapor only around its two cold eye points and transient vapor outline. T2–T5 become cremation-draft spirits through cindered shroud edges, heat-scaled chains, soot-dark hollow armor, ember seams confined to anchor objects, and rising hot smoke that preserves the footless silhouette.

The T1 Shade changes motion through a burn-and-cool eye cycle: its two points draw the transient vapor outline upward, flare at alignment, then contract to a dark eye gap. T2–T5 contract the upper body around a brazier-like hood or seal, expand chains with heat, mark emergence with directional smoke, and darken the active anchor during recovery.
counterplay: Leave the marked boundary, sever the motionless contacting link, or close on the stationary hilt while the blade is committed elsewhere; the other two chains continue orbiting but cannot strike. Affinity signal: For the T1 Shade, eye alignment completes the brief attack outline and the cooling eye gap remains hittable before the two points separate. T2–T5 turn the active chain or armor seal black after emergence; striking that cooling anchor prevents passage through the next surface.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only fire treatment without cindered material, heat-scaled anchors, and burn-cycle phasing
Glow-only fire treatment without a combustion route or cooling seal
A generic flame ghost that erases hood, shroud, chain, and empty lower silhouette
Fire emission that is indistinguishable from the family's small source-native eye lights
identityInvariants: A hooded or robed humanoid upper body becomes progressively defined while the lower body always trails into smoke or cold vapor without visible feet.
Black, charcoal, deep indigo, and ash grey carry one cold eye accent in pale blue, white, or sickly green; this family-native cold light is not an elemental affinity by itself.
Smoke, tattered shroud-cloth, cold vapor, rusted chain, and hollow armor preserve incorporeality through negative space and incomplete edges.
Chains, funeral shrouds, spectral crowns, and localized rings of source-native frost become anchors that explain when and where an otherwise incorporeal form can be opposed.
Escalation condenses a faint outline into a sharply defined regal silhouette while retaining a vapor tail, empty interior, and one readable anchor for every phase-through action.
telegraph: The visible skeletal hands reverse their grip, one orbiting chain stops against a surface, and cold light runs from the fixed link through the blade hilt before the remote edge appears.
